question.text: When the heat of a reaction at constant pressure is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi></math> and entropy change for the reaction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mo>deg</mo><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, it is predicted that the reaction at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>25</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Heat at constant pressure means enthalpy. i.e., ΔG=ΔH-TΔS

ΔH=2.5×103cal

ΔS=7.4caldeg-1

T=298 K

ΔG=ΔH-TΔS

=-25×103-298×7.4

=-4705.2 cal

As the value of ΔG is −4705.2 cal, which is a negative value, so this reaction will be spontaneous. 

Hence, the process is spontaneous.
